metric: deceleration the assumed service brake can hold against gravity
target: holds on a 25 % slope: brake deceleration >= g * sin(atan 0.25) = 2.38 m/s2
measured: assumed dry braking 2.50 m/s2 against 2.38 needed
note: margin 5 %. The winter planning value (1.50 m/s2) is the available friction on a slippery surface, not the brake's capacity, so it is not compared here. The brake itself has to be measured on the machine.

metric: stopping distance from the standard's test speed (top speed when below 32 km/h)
target: below the table limit; the limit formula must be read from the purchased standard
measured: twin stops from 19.8 km/h in 7.2 m after brake actuation (7.8 m with the retrofit actuator's delay)
note: Confirmed from the 1985 edition's sample: the test speed is 32 km/h or the top speed if lower, and the distance is measured from the point where the brake control is actuated. The limit table is not legible there and later editions are not free. The commonly quoted later form (v2/150 + 0.2(v + 5), v in km/h) gives 7.6 m, which the assumed braking would meet measured the standard's way; it corresponds to a mean deceleration of about 2.3 m/s2, close to the 2.5 m/s2 the stop budget assumes. To close: read the limit in the purchased standard and measure the machine's brake.

source: ISO 13855 (approach speed of a walking person)
metric: highest walking speed the adversarial search and the shifts use
measured: adversarial walker speeds up to 2.0 m/s
note: The fields are sized for the machine's stopping distance, as ISO 3691-4 does; a person walking into a machine that has already stopped is outside the stop function.

metric: a standing test piece (200 mm diameter) just inside the far edge of each protective field
target: detected in every field set, on the axis and at both far corners
measured: 129 of 129 test-piece positions detected in 43 field sets; 0 field sample points outside rated coverage
note: 2D twin; a return counts only inside a sensor's rated coverage. The front and rear fields end up to 8.1 m from the scanners, beyond their 4 m rated range, so three 9 m safety radars per end watch the far part (8.1 m at most); the scanners keep the side, contact and under-bucket fields. With the scanners alone the forward cap would be 0.31 m/s. The radar is rated for people, not for the test piece, and its use on a moving outdoor machine is to be confirmed with the manufacturer; the check on the hardware is test T4.

metric: scan plane height against the lying test piece
target: scan plane at or below 70 mm, or another means of detecting a person lying down
measured: scan plane 0.5 m on the full machine; no rated means of detecting a person lying on the ground
note: Decided: accepted as a stated residual risk (safety concept, residual risk 11). A scan plane at 70 mm cannot be used on a loader: on gravel and ruts it would see the ground. ISO 3691-4 is written for driverless trucks on flat floors; for autonomous earth-moving machines ISO 17757 relies on a controlled autonomous operating zone. Measures: access control to the operating area (A1). The autonomy side's 3D lidar and camera are the only sensors that could see a person on the ground; they are not safety rated and that case is not tested. The 1:8 testbed's plane is about 0.085 m, so test T4.2 shows the limit rather than hiding it.

metric: rated operating load against the full-turn static tipping load and a bucket of sand
target: rated load = 50 % of the tipping load and >= the struck bucket of sand
measured: rated load 9.1 kg, tipping load 18.21 kg, bucket of sand 8.2 kg
note: From CAD mass properties; weigh the built machine to confirm.

metric: PL of the stop function from component data
target: PL d calculated from the selected components' MTTFd, DC and CCF
measured: selected parts add up to 3.63e-07 1/h of the 1e-06 PL d limit; 6.37e-07 1/h left for the parts not selected
note: 4 safety laser scanners 3.20e-07; output stage: brake valve and drive cut-off, two monitored channels 4.29e-08. Output stage MTTFd 100 years per channel at 28000 operations a year; common-cause score claimed 95 (65 needed). Not selected, so no figure: safety radar system (6 sensors, 1 control unit); safety controller. PL d holds if those stay inside the remaining budget. Table K.1 values are from a manufacturer's reproduction and need confirming in the standard. kauha/safety/pl.py.

source: Dadhich et al. 2019, Volvo L180H field test (expert fills in 6-8 s; automatic 26 % longer)
metric: mean fill time and fill factor of the learned policy on the held-out test episodes
target: fill time <= 1.26 x 7 s = 8.8 s and fill factor >= 0.90
measured: fill time 8.7 s, fill factor 0.94 (200 held-out episodes)
note: Simulated bucket-pile model against a field result on a larger machine (L180H); it shows the policy is in the published range, not that the model is right.

source: Aoshima & Servin 2024, WA320-7: simulation differs from the machine by about 11 % in force
metric: learned policy on gravel with digging resistance 11 % lower and 11 % higher
target: fill factor >= 0.85 and every episode completes in both cases
measured: resistance x0.89: fill 1.03, 9.2 s, success 100 %; resistance x1.00: fill 1.02, 9.6 s, success 100 %; resistance x1.11: fill 1.00, 9.8 s, success 100 %
note: Covers the published sim-to-real force error as a change in digging resistance only.

source: Frank et al. 2012, 73 operators on a Volvo loader, short loading cycle
metric: KAUHA cycle time against the measured novice-to-professional spread
target: reported against the spread; the paper gives it only in plots
measured: KAUHA median cycle 70 s (truck loading, twin); every operator in the study's plots is below about 45 s
note: The study gives cycle times only in figures 9 and 10, whose axis ends near 45 s, and reports spread as ratios: productivity differs by a factor of 5 to 8 between operators, 2 to 4 without novices. So the twin's autonomous cycle is at least 1.5 times as long as a human short loading cycle. The causes are the 3 m/s speed cap from the protective field length and a longer travel path in the twin's site. The honest claim is unattended running, not speed. A like-for-like figure needs the pilot site's own operator timing.

source: Tampere University, 6 t wheel loader short Y-cycle recording (CC BY 4.0)
metric: twin driven with the recorded operator inputs: cylinder trajectories and phase durations
note: The recording's channel list is in its documentation PDF, which could not be read from the build environment. The replay will be written against that list, not guessed.

source: attack classes of the ROAD CAN dataset: fabrication, fuzzing, replay, masquerade, suspension
metric: attack frames accepted by the gateway or the PLC, and unsafe commands that follow
target: 0 forged frames accepted; replay and suspension end in a stop within the frame timeout
measured: from the open segment, through the segment guard: fuzzing 0 of 200000 forged frames forwarded; replay 0 of 20000 accepted; masquerade: gateway released in 0 of 400 cycles while the PLC said stop, 0 forged heartbeats accepted; suspension: brake after 0.105 s
note: The bus is split: the PLC, sensors and gateway are on a safety segment inside the cabinet; the autonomy computer, remote link and zone source are on an open segment. The guard forwards only four command frames from the open segment, each authenticated with an AES-128 CMAC, a freshness counter and a per-power-cycle session key. Under fuzzing 96 % of genuine commands still got through; the rest are lost and end in a stop by timeout. Limits: a compromised autonomy computer holds its own key and can send any command, which the PLC bounds as before. An attacker with a tool inside the cabinet is on the safety segment, where the CRC alone does not stop forged frames (82 of 200000 random frames accepted at a receiver); that is covered by physical access control, not by the bus. Reference implementation and firmware port, tested against each other; not yet run on the hardware.

metric: real vehicle traffic replayed onto the KAUHA bus, as recorded and remapped onto KAUHA identifiers
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_ROAD to a folder of candump logs.

metric: person recall and precision at confidence 0.25
target: recall >= 0.80, precision >= 0.75 (the values measured on Construction-PPE)
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_SODA to a YOLO-layout copy (images/, labels/).

metric: frames with a protective field occupied although no labelled object is inside it
target: false-occupied rate reported per sensor; target below 1 % of frames after the dust filter
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_LIDARDUSTX to the dataset folder (research-use licence).

metric: share of frames with a 4 m field ahead occupied, snow against clear runs of one route
target: snow adds less than 1 percentage point
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_BOREAS to a folder with two subfolders, snow/ and clear/, each holding Boreas sequences of the same route (boreas-YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM/lidar/*.bin). Optional KAUHA_BOREAS_SENSOR_HEIGHT in metres (default 2.0).

metric: labelled pedestrians a CFAR detector finds on the radar image in fog and snow
target: at least 90 % of those within 9 m
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_RADIATE to a folder of RADIATE sequences (each with Navtech_Cartesian/*.png and annotations/annotations.json); fog and snow sequences are the ones of interest. Needs Pillow.

metric: position error and time to declare the position invalid
note: The benchmark's download page and file format could not be read from the build environment. Needs the format description, then the EKF run on its logged GNSS and IMU instead of the twin's.
